en.title: Distance to the Nearest Fibonacci Number
en.description:
The Fibonacci numbers start from 0 and 1, and each later term is the sum of the previous two. Given a non-negative integer N, output the absolute difference to the nearest Fibonacci number; output only the distance, not the number itself.

The standard input, this site's constraints, the examples, and the test data were independently compiled by CSWork.
en.explanation:
Example 1: 25 lies between 21 and 34, at distances 4 and 9 respectively, so the answer is 4.

Example 2: 5 is itself a Fibonacci number, so the distance is 0.

Example 3: 0 is the first term of the sequence, so the distance is 0.
hints: Generate consecutive Fibonacci numbers until the later one is not less than N; compare the distances from these two numbers to N.
